evidence: Codex execution failures are surfaced with incompatible contracts across sibling modules: `call_codex.call_codex()` returns `CodexResult.error`, while `codex_lm.CodexLM.forward()` raises `RuntimeError` for the same subprocess failure classes.

`dspy_reviewers.run_dspy_review()` captures all reviewer exceptions into result values, then `prediction_to_review_output()` converts exceptions into free-form text (`DSPY_EXECUTION_FAILED`) instead of a structured failure object, making downstream handling format-dependent.

`collect_training.py` and `backfill_training.py` perform direct `read_text()` I/O without CLI-level error translation, while `find_plan.py`/`parse_verification.py` explicitly convert failures into user-facing error payloads and exit codes.

DSPy results are converted from structured prediction -> markdown text in `prediction_to_review_output()` -> parsed back to structure with `parse_findings()` in `run_parallel_reviews_dspy()`, creating a fragile translation loop.
Two parallel-review paths (`run_parallel_reviews` and `run_parallel_reviews_dspy`) duplicate orchestration/aggregation behavior instead of sharing a single backend-independent flow.

`aggregate_findings.aggregate_findings()` accepts multiple ad-hoc input shapes (`results` wrapper or raw dict) and relies on nested `.get(...)` access, signaling weak inter-script interface contracts.
`dspy_reviewers.py` hardcodes persistent state paths under `~/.claude/skills/fando-plan`, introducing an external environment dependency not declared/configured by CLI args or project config.
Review pipeline depends on text protocol coupling between modules (markdown format expectations) rather than stable typed objects, making module dependency edges brittle to formatting changes.
Optional DSPy dependency is guarded, but downstream behavior still tightly depends on specific persisted JSON module artifacts and path conventions.

fando-plan/scripts/dspy_reviewers.py mixes at least five concerns in one module: domain prompt/signature definitions (lines 66-350), runtime parallel orchestration (411-483), output normalization (490-525), training metric/label semantics (554-769), and persistence/CLI utilities (777-949).

fando-plan/scripts/run_parallel_reviews.py duplicates review lifecycle logic across codex and dspy paths (run_single_review at 101-173 vs run_parallel_reviews_dspy at 247-306), then adds a third aggregation/rendering layer in the same file (309-500).

The PROFILES registry in fando-plan/scripts/detect_profiles.py (29-110) is reused by unrelated workflows: runtime reviewer selection and prompt metadata (171-193, used by run_parallel_reviews.py) and training backfill domain labeling (fando-plan/scripts/backfill_training.py 21-40, 171-181), coupling independent policies through one mutable keyword table.

findings.summary: Codex subprocess failures use conflicting contracts across shared call paths.
evidence: `call_codex.py` models failures as data (`CodexResult.error` and `(None, error)` tuple from `run_codex_subprocess`).
`codex_lm.py` wraps the same subprocess classes (`TimeoutExpired`, `FileNotFoundError`, non-zero return code) as raised `RuntimeError` exceptions.
`dspy_reviewers.run_dspy_review()` then catches broad exceptions and stores them as values, creating a third failure channel.
findings.suggestion: Define one shared error contract for Codex invocation (for example, a typed `CodexExecutionError` hierarchy or a single Result object), and update `call_codex`, `CodexLM`, and DSPy orchestration to propagate that contract unchanged.

findings.summary: Reviewer execution exceptions are smuggled into normal review text output.
evidence: `run_dspy_review()` captures exceptions into `results[profile]` instead of failing fast or returning structured failure metadata.
`prediction_to_review_output()` converts exceptions into a synthetic markdown payload (`Error: DSPY_EXECUTION_FAILED: ...`) in the summary block, not a typed error object.
Training collection/backfill paths ingest review text as data, so this design can blend runtime failures with model content rather than enforcing an explicit failure boundary.
findings.suggestion: Return a structured per-profile status object (e.g., `{ok: bool, prediction, error_code, error_message}`) and make downstream collectors reject/branch on `ok == false` instead of parsing error text from markdown.

findings.summary: CLI scripts inconsistently handle file I/O failures at boundaries.
evidence: `collect_training.py` reads `plan_before`/`plan_after` with `read_text()` without handling `OSError`/decode failures, so failures escape as tracebacks.
`backfill_training.py` parser helpers (`parse_zellij_bridge`, `parse_jj_workspace`) call `read_text()` without localized error translation.
`find_plan.py` handles read failures explicitly and returns user-readable error messages, showing a different boundary policy for similar filesystem operations.
findings.suggestion: Add consistent boundary wrappers for file reads in the plan/training CLIs that catch `OSError` and decode errors, emit standardized error messages, and exit with predictable codes.

findings.summary: Optimized-module load failures are downgraded to silent fallback behavior.
evidence: `load_optimized_module()` catches broad exceptions and returns `None`, including unexpected loader failures.
`run_dspy_review()` treats `None` as normal and silently continues with unoptimized modules when `use_optimized=True`.
This creates a hidden runtime mode switch (optimized -> baseline) without surfacing an actionable failure to callers.
findings.suggestion: Differentiate not-found vs load-failed outcomes (e.g., enum/status object), and propagate load-failed as a surfaced warning/error path so callers can choose fail-fast or explicit degraded-mode execution.

findings.summary: DSPy output is serialized to markdown then reparsed, adding low-value indirection and contract fragility.
evidence: `prediction_to_review_output()` builds `## Findings` markdown text from structured prediction fields.
`run_parallel_reviews_dspy()` immediately feeds that text into `parse_findings()` to recover structured counts/items.
findings.suggestion: Return a typed findings object directly from DSPy path (or a shared dataclass schema) and use text formatting only for terminal rendering.

findings.summary: Codex and DSPy review runners duplicate result aggregation logic, increasing drift risk.
evidence: `run_parallel_reviews()` and `run_parallel_reviews_dspy()` both perform per-profile timing, error handling, count aggregation, and `ParallelReviewResult` mutation.
Backend-specific branches differ in subtle failure interpretation (exception object vs formatted error marker), making behavior consistency hard to maintain.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared backend-agnostic aggregation pipeline with a single normalized backend result interface.

findings.summary: Inter-script contracts rely on loose nested dicts instead of explicit schemas.
evidence: `aggregate_findings()` accepts either wrapped or raw input and reads nested keys via `.get`, defaulting missing severity to `UNKNOWN`.
Producer (`run_parallel_reviews.py`) emits a specific nested JSON structure, but consumer has no strict validation/versioning and silently tolerates shape drift.
findings.suggestion: Define a shared typed schema (dataclass/Pydantic-style validation) for review-result payloads and validate on load before aggregation.

findings.summary: Reviewer state storage is coupled to a hardcoded `~/.claude` path, reducing portability and reproducibility.
evidence: `SKILL_DIR = Path("~/.claude/skills/fando-plan").expanduser()` is fixed at import time.
Optimized/training state load-save behavior depends on that path and implicit file layout, but CLI in `run_parallel_reviews.py` does not expose configuration for this dependency.
findings.suggestion: Inject state directories via CLI/env/config with repository-local defaults, and centralize dependency path resolution in one configuration module.

findings.summary: Core reviewer module conflates signatures, orchestration, scoring, storage, and CLI concerns.
evidence: dspy_reviewers.py defines domain prompt/signature classes (66-350) and also owns training metric + labeling heuristics (554-769), save/load persistence (777-890), and its own CLI (898-949).

Other scripts import disjoint subsets from the same file for unrelated workflows: optimize.py imports optimization/training helpers; collect_training.py imports collection/persistence; run_parallel_reviews.py imports runtime review functions.
findings.suggestion: Split `dspy_reviewers.py` into bounded modules (e.g., `review_signatures.py`, `review_runtime.py`, `training_metric.py`, `training_store.py`) and keep only a thin compatibility facade for existing imports during migration.

findings.summary: Parallel review pipeline is duplicated per backend, creating drift-prone control flow.
evidence: run_parallel_reviews.py has separate backend paths that each perform execution, error mapping, parse_findings invocation, and severity aggregation (101-173 and 247-306).

The DSPy path relies on string pattern checks (`"Error:"` and exact section text) to detect failure states (286-289), while codex path uses structured `CodexResult.error`, showing divergent contracts.
Both paths then feed near-identical summary and output assembly logic (460-490), increasing update cost when output schema changes.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a backend adapter contract returning a normalized `ReviewResult` (success/error/findings/output), then run one shared aggregation/output path independent of backend type.

findings.summary: One keyword registry is serving incompatible responsibilities across runtime and training.
evidence: detect_profiles.PROFILES combines detection keywords with UI/prompt metadata (`display_name`, `prompt_file`) in a single structure (29-110).

backfill_training.classify_domain() reuses the same keyword list for post-hoc training label assignment (21-40), even though that task has different precision/recall tradeoffs than runtime reviewer routing.

run_parallel_reviews.py also uses PROFILES for display names and fallback prompt composition (132-133, 314-315), so edits to keywording can unintentionally affect training labels and user-facing behavior.
findings.suggestion: Separate `PROFILES` into explicit configuration layers: `reviewer_catalog` (display/prompt/runtime), `routing_keywords`, and `training_labeling_rules` with independent thresholds/weights and ownership.
